_readme: A10 (the DEMO half) — THE `chrome` APP IS BORN INSTALLED, PLACED **AND FILLED IN**.
★★ THE ACHIEVEMENT IS THE THIRD VERB, and the achado that produced this file is about usability, not
about apps: «eu instalei, apareceu os blocos lá no compose, mas eu não sei bem pra onde arrastar» — said
by the person who DESIGNED the product. A lojista would not have had a chance. ⇒ AN APP INSTALLED AND
EMPTY TEACHES LESS THAN NO APP AT ALL, because it adds five things to drag and no example of where they
go. The demo is also a living tutorial, so it has to show the finished state.
⚠️ MEASURED 2026-09-04 ON THE BENCH, and every number here is why the file exists:
· `chrome` was installed in BOTH tenants — by HAND, at 19:14 and 20:39, while somebody was testing.
Nothing in any seed installs it, and it is not in the platform seeder's list either.
· the shoe tenant carried SEVEN placements, all with test content (`"back":"a"`, `"seal":"c"`,
`"title":"2"`), and the coffee tenant carried ZERO. So the café's checkout and account screens wear
the REFERENCE mark today — our wordmark, in somebody else's shop, which is the exact outcome the app
exists to remove.
· installing it places NOTHING: the manifest declares `hooks: []`, so `seedDefaultPlacements` returns
immediately (packages/core/src/commands/extension.ts). Composing is not installing, and installing is
not placing. All three gestures are this file's.
★ THE FIVE BLOCKS AND THE FIVE SLOTS, read off the app's own manifest and confirmed against the
`target_override` column of the placements a human made on the bench:
checkout_header → storefront:checkout.header      account_header → storefront:account.header
checkout_footer → storefront:checkout.footer      account_footer → storefront:account.footer
brand           → storefront:header.brand
⛔ NOTHING WRITTEN ⇒ NOTHING DRAWN, and that is the app's decision, not a bug to work around. Every field
is optional and there is NO default word anywhere in it — a word nobody wrote would be this app choosing
Portuguese for somebody else's shop. So an unfilled block is an invisible one, which is precisely why a
demo that placed the blocks and left them empty would look like the app does nothing.
⚠️ `brand` REPLACES THE THEME'S WORDMARK rather than standing beside it (the kit's header cedes the mark
when something is placed in that slot). So a `brand` block with an empty config would DELETE the mark
from every page of the shop. Each entry below therefore carries either a logo or a word — never neither.
★★ pk19/D1 — THE WORDS THEMSELVES, REWRITTEN TO THE OWNER'S DICTATION (07/09). Everything above is about
the app being born placed; this pass is about what it SAYS. Four instructions, verbatim: the checkout
footer carries the payment methods on the left and a security line on the right; the account footer carries
a phone on the left and a contact e-mail in the middle; the account header says CARRINHO in the two shoe
stores and stays SACOLA in the café; and the checkout header is logo + step on the left with the way back
on the right.
⛔ AND THE EMPTIED FIELD IS DECLARED EMPTY, NEVER OMITTED. `planChrome`/`sameConfig` ask «is every key THIS
FILE states already stored with that value?» — a key the declaration drops is a key the comparison never
looks at, so deleting `middle_text` here would leave «Trocas e devoluções em até 30 dias» on an existing
box FOREVER and no birth would ever mention it. `""` is therefore an instruction and not a placeholder:
`wordOf` trims, so the area renders exactly as it would if the key were absent, and the difference is that
the seed now ASSERTS the absence. `seed/chrome.test.mjs` proves the omitted-key hole is real by driving
the plan over it.
⚠️ THE SHOE STORES SAID TWO WORDS FOR ONE THING, MEASURED: `seed/catalog.json` leaves `forge` and `outlet`
with an empty `vocabulary`, so their vitrine draws the kit's default — `Carrinho`
(packages/storefront-kit/src/vocabulary/vocabulary-keys.ts:52) — while this file wrote `Sacola` over the
account header of the same store. The café is the store that actually renamed the thing (`vocabulary.cart
= Sacola`) and is the one the owner told us to leave alone. So the instruction and the defect are the same
line, and the guard now ties the two files together instead of pinning a word.
★★ pk20/D1 — AND NOW THE SHOE STORES HAVE A MARK IN THE FUNNEL TOO, WHICH RETIRES BOTH OF THE REASONS
THIS FILE USED TO GIVE FOR THEM NOT HAVING ONE. Both are gone, and both were checked against the source
rather than assumed:
· «this repository has no mark for them» — it has, since this pass: `seed/photos/forge-store-logo.png`
and `seed/photos/forge-outlet-logo.png`, cut from the two stores' own rendered wordmarks on
transparent ground, named after `forge-co-logo.png` because that is the precedent the uploader reads
(`bin/seed.mjs:772` resolves a bare name inside `seed/photos/`).
· «a logo would DELETE «Voltar à loja» from the funnel» — TRUE when it was written, FALSE today. The
monorepo's half of R4 landed (`2eb9c56c2`, in `v03/integra`): `extensions/chrome/checkout-header.tsx`
now draws the mark, the step label and the way back as THREE positions (lines 63-100), and
`account-header.tsx:34-45` does the same with a divider between the mark and the way back. A logo and
a written word coexist; neither erases the other.
⛔ AND THE LOGO GOES IN THE TWO BARS ONLY — NEVER IN `brand`. That block is the one place where the two
are still exclusive: `extensions/chrome/brand.tsx:40-50` draws `logo.url ? : (text + tail)`, so a
logo in the shop's header would DELETE the wordmark the owner asked for in the same breath. The vitrine's
mark is TEXT on purpose — it re-tints itself with the theme's accent (`.tail` is `var(--color-accent)`,
chrome.module.css:148) and a raster does not.
★★ pk21/D3 — THE FUNNEL'S FOOTER GETS A PICTURE, WHICH IS THE HALF OF THIS APP THE DEMO HAD NEVER SHOWN.
Verbatim, 07/09: «compra segura precisa usar o do app, precisa preencher pois quero mostrar isso na demo».
Until now every `<area>_image` in this file was empty and the three footer areas only ever carried WORDS —
so an operator reading the demo learnt that a block holds text, and never that it holds art.
⚠️ AND THE PICTURE REPLACES THE WORD ON THE SCREEN, MEASURED — do not read `end_text` beside `end_image` as
two things drawn side by side. `footerArea` (extensions/chrome/logic.ts:53-61) returns
`{kind:'image', url, alt: text}` as soon as the image RESOLVED, and `footer-block.tsx:38-43` draws an
``: the area shows the picture and «Compra Segura» becomes its DESCRIPTION. That is the app's
declared contract and it says so in the Compose hint an operator reads («A imagem vence o texto; o texto
passa a ser a descrição dela»). ⇒ the word STAYS in the declaration for two reasons and neither is
decoration: it is the picture's only accessible name, and a key this file drops is a key no birth ever
corrects (see the `sameConfig` note above).
★★ pk22/D4 — AND THAT CONTRACT IS WHY THE SEAL IS NOW A LOCKUP: THE PADLOCK AND THE WORDS IN ONE ART.
pk21/D3 shipped the padlock alone and reported the consequence — image wins, so the shopper saw a stroke
and no promise in writing. The three ways out (only the icon · icon + word in one piece · the two side by
side, which the contract forbids in one area) went to the owner on 07/09 and he chose: «b está bom». The
two files are `compra-segura-lockup-escuro.png` (forge) and `compra-segura-lockup-claro.png` (outlet),
rendered INSIDE each shop's own checkout page, so each carries that shop's face — the reference theme's
Urbanist and the outlet's Figtree (themes/outlet/tokens.css:103) — at that page's real size. They are used
as delivered: not re-tinted, not resized, not standardised into one file.
⚠️ ONE THING WAS CHANGED IN THE BYTES AND IT IS NOT A RE-CUT: the two lockups arrived FLATTENED ONTO WHITE
(PNG colour type 2, no alpha), which `bin/chrome-seal-ink.guard.mjs` caught on the spot — «its commonest
opaque colour is only 86.6% of 177 408 opaque pixels». On the outlet that file would have been near-white
art inside its own opaque white slab on a #17181a footer. Every non-white pixel was exactly `a·ink +
(1-a)·white` (worst reconstruction error 1/255, measured), so the transparent original was recovered by
solving for the alpha: same ink, ground given back.
⚠️ AND THE CANVAS WAS THEN GROWN ON PURPOSE — 60 transparent rows above and 60 below, width untouched, no
pixel of ink moved. `.areaImage` clamps the HEIGHT and throws the file's own scale away (`max-height:
2.5em`, chrome.module.css:111-115), so the letters inside art like this are sized by `cap-height ÷ canvas`
— a property of the FILE. MEASURED: the capitals span 83 rows, which on the delivered 176-row canvas was
47.16% ⇒ 1.179em on screen, about 1.7× the words beside them. At 296 rows it is 28.04% ⇒ 0.7010em, parity
with the footer's own text — and, by a second and independent route, the scale the art was rendered at
(2.5 × 14.5 ÷ 296 = 0.1225 against the 0.125 of an 8× render). The clamp lives in the PRODUCT repository
and bending a general rule for one picture is how debt is invented, so the ART was fitted to the slot
instead. ⛔ It is NOT a dodge of `bin/chrome-seal-ink.guard.mjs`: every number the guard reads got worse,
not better — the aspect fell from 5.727 to 3.405, closer to the floor it has to clear.
★★ AND THERE ARE TWO FILES BECAUSE THE INK IS THE THEME'S. The art is a stroke and letters on a TRANSPARENT
ground, so it re-tints itself with nothing, while the footer's ink is
`var(--color-chrome-muted, var(--color-muted))` (chrome.module.css:98). MEASURED: the reference footer is
#ffffff with #4b4d52 ink; the outlet's is #17181a with #e4e6ea (themes/outlet/tokens.css:117-122). Hand one
shop the other's file and the lockup is dark art on a dark ground — still 200, still present in the DOM,
invisible. `bin/chrome-seal-ink.guard.mjs` decodes the PNG's own pixels and compares them with the theme's
token, so the tint is graded and not trusted to a filename; since pk22/D4 it also counts the ISLANDS of ink
(14 — the padlock's two plus twelve letters), which is what stops the lone padlock coming back unnoticed.
⛔ The café is NOT given one: it has a footer of its own and the owner did not name
it — and it is named in that guard's lists rather than left absent.
★★ pk21/D3, THE OTHER HALF — THE MARK IS LOWERCASE WHERE IT STANDS ALONE AS A MARK; PROSE KEEPS PORTUGUESE
CAPITALISATION. pk20 lowercased the two shops' headers and left the footers of the same shops signing off
as «Forge Outlet» and «Forge · calçados e acessórios» — one shop, two spellings of one name, a click apart.
Those two `account_footer.end_text` are the footer's SIGNATURE and are now the mark itself
(`forge.outlet`, `forge.store · calçados e acessórios`), graded against the `brand` block rather than pinned
as literals. ⚠️ THE RÉGUA WAS READ OFF THE STORE THE OWNER SAID WAS ALREADY RIGHT: the café already signed
`forge.co · café de origem`.
⛔ AND «Voltar ao Outlet» STAYS, JUDGED RATHER THAN SWEPT. It is a SENTENCE whose noun is the shop, not the
mark: «o Outlet» is a proper noun and takes a capital in Portuguese, lowercasing it would read as a typo,
and «Voltar ao forge.outlet» drops a domain-shaped token into a clause where it has no grammar. It is
pinned in `seed/chrome.test.mjs`'s dictation table so that staying is a decision and not a field nobody
looked at. ⚠️ The same régua also explains what this pass did NOT touch: `Forge Outlet` survives as the
store's registered NAME (seed/box.json:122, seed/catalog.json:55) and in ten CMS titles
(seed/outlet.json:410-453). Those are entity names and prose, never the mark.

forge._why: The reference shoe store. ★ pk20/D1 — IT NOW WEARS ITS MARK IN TWO PLACES AND IN TWO MEDIA, which is one decision and not two: the VITRINE keeps the mark as TEXT (`forge` + `.store`, the tail painted with the theme's accent) because that is the half that re-tints itself when the theme moves, and the CHECKOUT and ACCOUNT bars carry the same mark as a PICTURE, because those two bars have had room for a logo AND the way back since R4. The owner's two corrections are both here: minúsculo (`Forge` was a capital nobody had asked for) and the mark reaching the funnel at all («não aparece o logo no checkout e minha conta»). ★ pk19: `cart` is `Carrinho` because that is what this store's VITRINE already says (empty `vocabulary` in seed/catalog.json ⇒ the kit's default); it said `Sacola` here, which made one store use two words for one thing. ★ pk21/D3: the checkout footer's right-hand area is now a PICTURE, drawn in this footer's ink — #4b4d52 on the vanilla theme's white — with «Compra Segura» kept as its description; ★★ pk22/D4 REPLACED that picture with the LOCKUP (`compra-segura-lockup-escuro.png`: the padlock AND the words, in this shop's Urbanist at the checkout page's own size), because the image WINS the text and the padlock alone left the funnel with no promise in writing — the owner picked that shape out of three on 07/09 («b está bom»); and the account footer signs off with this shop's own mark instead of a capitalised one (`Forge · calçados e acessórios` → `forge.store · calçados e acessórios`).

outlet._why: The same brand under its own theme, and the mark is where that stops being a claim: `tail` is drawn in the theme's accent (carmine here, copper on the reference), so ONE placement makes the outlet look like the outlet without a line of code. ★★ pk20/D1 — AND THE TAIL IS `.outlet`, WITH A POINT, BECAUSE A SPACE CANNOT SURVIVE THE TRIP. It used to be `" Outlet"` and the shop's header read `ForgeOutlet`, glued: `wordOf` trims every configured word (`extensions/chrome/logic.ts:38`) and `brand.tsx` concatenates `text` and `tail` with nothing between them, so the separator has to be a CHARACTER. The point is also the shape the sibling stores' marks already have (`forge.store`, `forge.co`), which is what makes this the right mark rather than a workaround for a trim. The funnel's mark is the same wordmark as a picture, in this theme's own ink (#e4e6ea on #17181a, themes/outlet/tokens.css:117-120). ⚠️ pk19 TOOK THE SEAL OUT OF THE HEADER AND THE THREE INSTITUTIONAL SENTENCES OUT OF THE FOOTER: the owner called that content bad and dictated its replacement, and a store-specific promise («produtos originais com nota fiscal») is exactly the kind of claim he moved to one shared security line. The outlet keeps its own voice where he did not touch it — the way back, which stays «Voltar ao Outlet» because it is a sentence about the SHOP and not the mark. ★★ pk21/D3 CORRECTED THE OTHER HALF OF THAT SENTENCE: the footer's right-hand mark was still `Forge Outlet`, the exact glued capital pk20 removed from the header of the same shop, and it is now `forge.outlet`. And the checkout footer gains the seal in THIS theme's ink — #e4e6ea, because the escuro file would be dark art on this shop's #17181a footer. ★★ pk22/D4 made that seal the LOCKUP (`compra-segura-lockup-claro.png`), and it is a SECOND file rather than the forge's because it carries this shop's own face too: `themes/outlet/tokens.css:103` sets `--font-sans` to Figtree where the reference theme sets Urbanist, and the art was rendered inside this shop's checkout page.

cafe._why: ★ THE STORE THIS ITEM WAS REALLY ABOUT. Its vitrine is a FORK and wears its own chrome; its CHECKOUT and its ACCOUNT screens are ours, hosted, and until this file they wore the reference mark — the café's buyers reached the payment step under somebody else's wordmark. This is the one entry with a LOGO, because it is the one store whose logo this repository actually has: `seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png`, the same mark the forked storefront imports as a bundled file (storefront-coffee/src/components/coffee/CoffeeChrome.tsx). The fork owns its copy; the hosted funnel needs it as an ASSET, which is what `logo` is — a `type:'id'` reference the kernel resolves to a url at read time. ★ pk19: the one store whose `cart` STAYS `Sacola` — the owner named it («na de café deixa como está») and the dataset agrees with him: `cafe` is the only store that declares `vocabulary.cart = Sacola` in seed/catalog.json, so here the account header and the vitrine already said the same word. ★★ pk25/D2 — AND THE FILE BEHIND THAT `logo` WAS THE ARTBOARD EXPORT, WHICH IS WHY THE MARK LOOKED MINUSCULE. The bar sizes a logo BY HEIGHT ALONE (`.logo { height: 2em; width: auto }`, extensions/chrome/chrome.module.css:22-26, with the reason written beside it), so the FILE'S proportion decides how much ink the shopper sees. `seed/photos/forge-co-logo.png` was 1536x1024 with the wordmark sitting as an 856x231 island in the middle — 22.6% of the file's height — so at 2em the mark drew 0.451em tall. It is now the cut the owner delivered (898x273, same 856x231 of ink, 84.6% of the height, 1.692em drawn): SAME PIXELS, 3.75x the mark. ⚠️ AND THE CAUSE WAS A HALF-DONE FIX, not a bad export: the fork bundles its own copy of this same mark and s3-11 trimmed THAT one (storefront-coffee/.../forge-co-logo.png, 858x233) and wrote a guard to keep it trimmed, while this copy was left behind and graded by nobody — one shop drawing one mark correctly in its vitrine and a third of the size in its checkout. `bin/chrome-logo-crop.guard.mjs` now grades every declared `logo` by PROPORTION (never by filename) and ties the two copies of the café's mark together.

_balcao_why: ⛔ THE COUNTER GETS NO CHROME, AND IT IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY SKIPPED — the same rule
`seed/box.json` writes for the warming step: «a store simply absent from a report is indistinguishable
from one that failed, and this repository has already paid twice for a summary that was silent about what
MEASURED: all five chrome blocks declare `surface: 'storefront'` and render inside the two deployables a
browser reaches — the vitrine (`brand`) and the hosted checkout/account screens (the other four). The
counter is neither. It is a whole-host app of its own (caddy `:82`, no store in the URL), the shopper it
serves never types a `/s/<id>` URL, and it places its
orders through its own screens. Five placements there would render nowhere: rows in a Compose board that
an operator can move around and never see the effect of, which is a worse lesson than an empty board.
⇒ THE DEMO SHOWS THE APP IN THE THREE SHOPS A PERSON CAN OPEN. Wanting it on the counter as well is one
entry in `stores` above and no code change — that is what makes this a declaration rather than a decision
